newsitem.title: CHINA: FOCUS-China stocks fall on Hong Kong hangover.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-China stocks fall on Hong Kong hangover.

text.p: China's stock markets fell on Wednesday morning as euphoria surrounding the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule dissipated and investors waited for the post-handover trend to become clear, brokers said.
Shanghai domestic currency A shares fell about 2.9 percent to 1,268.73 points in late morning trading, while the foreign currency B shares were off 1.45 percent at 80.299 points.
"The Hong Kong handover was good for popular feeling, but it doesn't have much meaning for the market," said an analyst at China Southern Securities in Shanghai.
"With Hong Kong closed today, there is not a lot of foreign buying of the B shares," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai.
Shenzhen A shares also fell as investors wait for a clear post-handover trend to emerge, brokers said. The Shenzhen A index lost 3.87 percent to 432.03 points in late morning trade.

"The (Hong Kong) handover is now no longer a factor in the Shenzhen market because investors have already been preparing for the event for a long time," said a broker at China Guotai Securities in Shenzhen.
Brokers said they expected the markets to consolidate over the next few sessions as investors await fresh leads from the scheduled announcement of 1997 interim results in July and August.
